narrative.text:
I’ll inspect the repository guidance and both parents, resolve the merge, then run the required gates and document any failures against the parent results.The fork’s writability check makes a fresh Slack lookup to confirm membership, so it cannot finish before “any Slack API call.” I’ve asked for a decision on whether that authorization lookup may precede text validation. Meanwhile, the fork baseline passed: 731 tests passed, 23 skipped, none failed.The decision is to preserve the fork’s authorization-refusal order, allowing its existing read-only lookup before text validation. I also found two fork-only paths needing protection: explicit-policy DM sends and protected-file attachment framing. The targeted tests pass, including upstream’s new security and transport tests; I’m adding regression coverage for the fork paths and checking the dependency API changes.No blocking findings. Review saved to `$ORGASMIC_EVIDENCE_DIR/independent-review.md`.

Independent targeted probes: **57 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**. Verified fork framing coverage, protected fetch-reference usability, authorization precedence, and core 0.4.0 compatibility. No full suite repeated; final commit and clean-tree gates remain implementation responsibilities.The merge passes all 790 tests on Node 24, with none skipped. Independent review found no blocking issues. All six added regression tests also failed when the relevant protections were temporarily disabled, then passed after restoration. I’ll now create the single merge commit and rerun the required gates on that commit.
